newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Zhirinovsky says Libya's Gaddafi new idol.
newsitem.headline: Zhirinovsky says Libya's Gaddafi new idol.

text.p: Russian ultra-nationalist leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky said after a meeting with Libya's Muammar Gaddafi that the leader of the North African country was the new idol of people since the fall of communism, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Wednesday.
"(A)fter the fall of the dream of millions who followed communism, these are now attached to the person of Muammar Gaddafi and his thought," JANA quoted Zhirinovsky as saying after the meeting.

"With the leader Muammar Gaddafi efforts and his penetrating thought it will be possible to unify efforts between Arabs and Russians to create a new world situation in the confrontation with the colonialist pressures and to fight them," he added.

JANA, monitored in Tunis, said that Zhirinovsky made the statement after Gaddafi explained him a prophesy that the East, including Russia, China and the Moslem and Arab worlds, will set up a front against the West.
Zhirinovsky arrived on Monday night in Tripoli for his third visit to Libya, just as controversial U.S. Nation of Islam's leader Louis Farrakhan left Tripoli after meeting Gaddafi.

"Communists had raised the slogan of (handing) power to the people, but they gave nothing to the people. Gaddafi made so much, not only for his people, but also for all oppressed in the world," he said.
Zhirinovsky renewed his condemnation of the United Nations Security Coucil sanctions imposed on Libya since 1992 over the Lockerbie affair.
Libya is under U.N. sanctions for failing to hand over to the United States or Britain two Libyan suspects in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, that killed 270 people.
Zhirinovsky last visit to Libya and meeting with Gaddafi was in March 1996, a few weeks before he ran in the June elections against President Boris Yeltsin.
